title: RFI's seismic early-warning system on the Rome-Naples high-speed line, operational since 3 May 2025, stops trains preventively during a magnitude 4.4 earthquake
summary: euronews (15 Jul 2025): about 20 accelerometric stations over 200 km feed software that analyzes P-waves and automatically slows or stops trains; in the weeks after activation a magnitude 4.4 quake...
account: ANSA reported on 14 Jul 2025 that Ferrovie dello Stato's infrastructure company Rete Ferroviaria Italiana had activated Italy's first seismic early-warning system on the Rome-Naples high-speed line, developed with the Physics Department of the University of Naples Federico II and with technical support from the Railway Technical Research Institute of the Japanese railways; a network of latest-generation sensors detects the earliest seismic waves and within seconds automatically activates safety protocols to slow or stop trains. euronews (15 Jul 2025) added that the system comprises about 20 seismic stations along 200 km, on the surface and in deep boreholes, linked by an SDH fiber network, that an advanced software intelligence instantly analyzes the data and assesses the quake's danger, that it had been operational since 3 May 2025 and that in the following weeks it was tested by a magnitude 4.4 earthquake, during which trains on the Rome-Naples line were stopped preventively. Neither article gives the date of that earthquake, so the date given is that of FS's announcement reported by ANSA. ANSA does not mention artificial intelligence; the OECD AI Incidents Monitor lists the system (2025-07-14-dd98) as AI-powered and a protective response.
purpose: The system is built to detect the first seismic waves and automatically slow or stop high-speed trains before stronger shaking arrives.
system: RFI seismic early-warning system (Early Warning Sismico) on the Rome-Naples high-speed line
developer: Rete Ferroviaria Italiana with the Physics Department of the University of Naples Federico II and JR RTRI
taxonomy_note: An automatic train stop on P-wave detection is a failsafe; no harm averted is documented.

ratings.reason: Precautionary stops were executed automatically during a magnitude 4.4 quake; no damage, derailment or delay figures are reported.
No passenger outcome is documented beyond the stops.

ai_role.statement: The software evaluated the seismic signals and triggered the stop protocol without human intervention, per euronews; the sources are two Italian news reports of the company's announcement, with no RFI document fetched and no description of the algorithm.

produced_by: Dense accelerometric stations along a high-speed line in a seismic region
Automatic P-wave analysis with thresholds tied to train control
must_hold: P-waves arrive early enough before damaging shaking to brake trains
False triggers stay rare enough to keep the automatic stop enabled

headline: RFI seismic warning stops Rome-Naples trains in a 4.4 quake
